Commentary.Commentary: More action to come - That's the warm-up games done and dusted for these two sides, and the attention now shifts to the main event. Scotland open their campaign in Manchester on Saturday, 13 June, against Ireland, while Pakistan face arch-rivals India in Birmingham on Sunday, 14 June. We are not done for the day yet here in Derby, though. Up next at 2 pm GMT, the Netherlands square off against Sri Lanka. Let's hope the weather clears up by then. It's goodbye for now.

Kathryn led the way - After being asked to bat first, Scotland found life difficult early on a sticky wicket, but they grew in confidence as the innings progressed. Darcey Carter played her part, but it was Kathryn Bryce who stole the show. Dropped on 6, the Scottish skipper made Pakistan pay dearly with a 43-ball 94. With the ball, Pakistan were impressive in patches, but it all unravelled towards the back end of the innings. Fielding lapses began to creep in, and Scotland capitalised on those opportunities to finish strongly.

A chase that never took off -  In pursuit of a daunting total, Pakistan could never really get going with the bat. The intent was certainly there, but the loss of three wickets inside the Powerplay made an already difficult chase even tougher. Scotland continued to hold their own outside the Powerplay and never allowed Pakistan any breathing room. A lot rested on Fatima Sana's shoulders to pull her side back into the contest, but the rain denied the skipper any opportunity to mount a serious challenge.

That's that for the game - The weather has had the final say, with no further play possible. Scotland win this contest by 41 runs on the DLS method and make it two wins from two in their warm-up fixtures. That will give Kathryn Bryce and her side plenty of belief and confidence heading into the main event. As for Pakistan, they have now lost both their warm-up games. More than anything, the Asian side will need to sharpen up in the field if they are to compete against the stronger teams in the competition.

12.30 pm GMT - Right on cue, the rain has arrived. There is a strong wind as well, and the ground staff are having to battle the elements as they rush to bring the covers on and protect the run-up areas. The chances of us having any more play in this fixture appear rather slim at the moment, but let's hope for the best.

12.24 pm GMT - We have some news. It seems the match officials are not quite satisfied with the conditions just yet. They have decided to hold another inspection at 12.35 pm GMT. Well, we thought the hover cover was about to be removed, but instead, the ground staff are rolling the square covers back on. It is looking rather dark in the distance, and perhaps the ground staff have spotted another shower on the radar heading this way.

12.17 pm GMT - An inspection is currently underway as the match officials stroll across the outfield. The mop-up work continues as well. Encouragingly, the end of the ground that looked particularly threatening earlier is also beginning to clear up. With conditions continuing to improve, we should not be too far away from a resumption.

12 pm GMT - It has stopped raining. The square covers are starting to come off, but the hover cover is yet to be removed. That caution is understandable given that one side of the ground is still looking rather ominous, with plenty of dark clouds. We still have one more game scheduled later in the day here in Derby, between the Netherlands and Sri Lanka, and the forecast suggests we should be just fine for that contest.

11.50 am GMT - The covers are still on, but there are at least some encouraging signs. The skies appear noticeably brighter than they did a little while ago, and just as we type, the sun is out. The ground staff have sprung into action, with the hover cover now being powered up to take it off the playing surface. In the meantime, you can switch tabs and follow the action from the other warm-up game currently underway between Bangladesh and Ireland, which is going right down to the wire.

11.30 am GMT - The rain has picked up, and off go the players. The hover cover has been brought on to cover the playing surface. Andrew Leonard mentions that this spell of rain is expected to last 30 minutes according to the radar. He further informs us that Pakistan are currently 42 runs behind on DLS. Should there be no further play, Scotland would be declared the winners. Stay tuned for further updates.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Scotland Women were 41/0 at the end of the Powerplay, while Pakistan are 45/3. The intent has certainly been there from Pakistan's batters, but they have found it difficult to strike the ball cleanly on this surface. Scotland, meanwhile, will be looking to tighten their grip on the contest even further. Well, this is not a great sign as the wind has picked up, and it has gone dark overhead. It will be pace after the break in the form of Chloe Abel.
